summary: Polybus (Ancient Greek: Πόλυβος) son of Antenor is a Trojan prince who stands with Hector, Polydamas, Aeneas, and his brothers Agenor and Acamas when battle rages about the ships. Quintus Smyrnaeus also places him among Antenor's sons. He is distinct from Polybus of Corinth (Oedipus' foster-father) and from Penelope's Ithacan and Zacynthian suitors of the same name.

sections.heading: Antenorid at Troy
paragraphs: Iliad 11.59–71 gathers the Trojans about Hector, Polydamas, Aeneas, and Antenor's three sons — Polybus, goodly Agenor, and young Acamas. Homer fixes this Polybus among the Dardanian princes rather than among Ithaca's wooers.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (polybus-antenorid) is Antenor's Trojan son. Distinct from polybus-ithaca and polybus-zacynthus (Penelope's suitors), from Corinth's foster-father of Oedipus, and from other Polybus kings and craftsmen on the Wikipedia disambiguation page.
